claim: The Fly Cell Atlas encompasses the entire fly, covering the entire head and body, in addition to all major organs.
source: This single-nuclei atlas encompasses the entire fly, covering the entire head and body, in addition to all major organs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the Fly Cell Atlas.

claim: The Fly Cell Atlas catalogs many hundreds of cell types, of which 250 were annotated.
source: This atlas catalogs many hundreds of cell types, of which we annotated 250.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: A large number of clusters in the Fly Cell Atlas remain to be fully characterized, particularly in the brain.
source: Thus, a large number of clusters remain to be fully characterized, in particular in the brain.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: Single-nuclei sequencing results in loss of information about the spatial location of cells in the body.
source: Furthermore, by applying single-nuclei sequencing, all information about the spatial location of the cells in the body and of about possible subcellular localization of the mRNAs within these cells is lost.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a limitation of single-nuclei sequencing.

claim: Single-nuclei sequencing results in loss of information about possible subcellular localization of mRNAs within cells.
source: Furthermore, by applying single-nuclei sequencing, all information about the spatial location of the cells in the body and of about possible subcellular localization of the mRNAs within these cells is lost.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a limitation of single-nuclei sequencing.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics was applied using a selected gene panel to pinpoint the locations of 150 mRNA species in the adult fly.
source: In a proof-of-concept study, we have here applied spatial transcriptomics using a selected gene panel to pinpoint the locations of 150 mRNA species in the adult fly.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the study.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics enabled mapping of unknown clusters identified in the Fly Cell Atlas to their spatial locations in the fly brain.
source: This enabled us to map unknown clusters identified in the Fly Cell Atlas to their spatial locations in the fly brain.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics discovered principles of mRNA localization in large and crowded muscle cells.
source: Additionally, spatial transcriptomics discovered interesting principles of mRNA localization and transcriptional diversity within the large and crowded muscle cells that may spark future mechanistic investigations.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics discovered transcriptional diversity within large and crowded muscle cells.
source: Additionally, spatial transcriptomics discovered interesting principles of mRNA localization and transcriptional diversity within the large and crowded muscle cells that may spark future mechanistic investigations.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a result of the study.

claim: Single-cell technologies have revolutionized biological research by allowing study of complex tissues with unprecedented resolution.
source: Single-cell technologies have revolutionized biological research, allowing researchers for the first time to study complex tissues with unprecedented resolution (Klein et al., 2015), leading to the creation of tissue-specific atlases (Schaum et al., 2018; The Tabula Sapiens Consortium, 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Upon tissue dissociation into single cells, the spatial context of the cell in the organism is lost.
source: However, upon tissue dissociation into single cells, the spatial context of the cell in the organism and of the mRNAs within the cell is lost, since all data of the cell are compressed into one multidimensional data point.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as a limitation of single-cell technologies.

claim: The localization of a cell type within a tissue can inform about the function of the cell.
source: This is a significant drawback, as the localization of a cell type within a tissue can inform about the function of this cell (Tomancak et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Many mRNAs show subcellular localization patterns that may have functional roles.
source: Furthermore, many mRNAs show subcellular localization patterns that may have functional roles (Jambor et al., 2015; Lécuyer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Spatially resolved transcriptomics can circumvent the loss of spatial information that occurs with single-cell dissociation.
source: This loss of information can be circumvented using spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: In SRT, spatial information of RNA species is determined through spatially localized barcoded DNA arrays with or without microfluidics, followed by sequencing.
source: In SRT, spatial information of the RNA species is determined either through the use of spatially localized barcoded DNA arrays with or without the use of microfluidics, followed by sequencing (Rodriques et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2022), or by imaging using multiplexed rounds of single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) methods.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In SRT, spatial information of RNA species is determined by imaging using multiplexed rounds of single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) methods.
source: In SRT, spatial information of the RNA species is determined either through the use of spatially localized barcoded DNA arrays with or without the use of microfluidics, followed by sequencing (Rodriques et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2022), or by imaging using multiplexed rounds of single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) methods.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Barcoded sequencing approaches allow unbiased mapping of all transcripts.
source: While barcoded sequencing approaches allow unbiased mapping of all transcripts, their spatial resolution is, in general, lower (Moses and Pachter, 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Barcoded sequencing approaches have lower spatial resolution in general.
source: While barcoded sequencing approaches allow unbiased mapping of all transcripts, their spatial resolution is, in general, lower (Moses and Pachter, 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Multiplexed smFISH identifies the position of each RNA molecule independently at a high spatial resolution.
source: Multiplexed smFISH identifies the position of each RNA molecule independently at a high spatial resolution, but it is limited in throughput to a few genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Multiplexed smFISH is limited in throughput to a few genes.
source: Multiplexed smFISH identifies the position of each RNA molecule independently at a high spatial resolution, but it is limited in throughput to a few genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Technical breakthroughs have increased the number of genes that can be analyzed by multiplexed smFISH to several hundred through the use of barcoding.
source: Recently, technical breakthroughs have been presented to increase the number of genes to several hundred through the use of barcoding (Chen et al., 2015; Eng et al., 2019; Lubeck et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The adult fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster is a widely used model for cell biology, neurobiology, physiology and behavior.
source: The adult fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster is a widely used model for cell biology, neurobiology, physiology and behavior (Sokolowski, 2001; Grenier and Leulier, 2020; Benton, 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The entire adult fly cell atlas (FCA) was recently completed.
source: The recent completion of the entire adult fly cell atlas (FCA) (Li et al., 2022), and the aging fly cell atlas (Lu et al., 2023) provided an in-depth annotation of various cell types, however without information about the localization of these cells or their mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The FCA provided an in-depth annotation of various cell types without information about the localization of these cells or their mRNAs.
source: The recent completion of the entire adult fly cell atlas (FCA) (Li et al., 2022), and the aging fly cell atlas (Lu et al., 2023) provided an in-depth annotation of various cell types, however without information about the localization of these cells or their mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Many single-cell clusters in the FCA were left unannotated although marker genes were identified.
source: In addition, many single-cell clusters were left unannotated although marker genes were identified.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: In tubular head and leg muscles, the nuclei are located in a central row surrounded by contractile myofibrils.
source: In tubular head and leg muscles, the nuclei are located in a central row surrounded by contractile myofibrils, while in fibrillar indirect flight muscles (IFMs), the nuclei are organized in multiple rows between the myofibril bundles (Luis and Schnorrer, 2021; Schönbauer et al., 2011), distributed along the length of the large 1 mm long fibers (Spletter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In fibrillar indirect flight muscles (IFMs), the nuclei are organized in multiple rows between the myofibril bundles.
source: In tubular head and leg muscles, the nuclei are located in a central row surrounded by contractile myofibrils, while in fibrillar indirect flight muscles (IFMs), the nuclei are organized in multiple rows between the myofibril bundles (Luis and Schnorrer, 2021; Schönbauer et al., 2011), distributed along the length of the large 1 mm long fibers (Spletter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IFM nuclei are distributed along the length of the large 1 mm long fibers.
source: In tubular head and leg muscles, the nuclei are located in a central row surrounded by contractile myofibrils, while in fibrillar indirect flight muscles (IFMs), the nuclei are organized in multiple rows between the myofibril bundles (Luis and Schnorrer, 2021; Schönbauer et al., 2011), distributed along the length of the large 1 mm long fibers (Spletter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The organization of nuclei in muscle cells is thought to optimize mRNA distribution by minimizing transport distances.
source: This organization is thought to optimize the mRNA distribution by minimizing transport distances (Bruusgaard et al., 2003) and misalignment of the nuclei has been linked to severe myopathies in humans (Folker and Baylies, 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Misalignment of nuclei in muscle cells has been linked to severe myopathies in humans.
source: This organization is thought to optimize the mRNA distribution by minimizing transport distances (Bruusgaard et al., 2003) and misalignment of the nuclei has been linked to severe myopathies in humans (Folker and Baylies, 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Molecular Cartography is a multiplexed single-molecule hybridization method with submicron resolution (~136 nm).
source: Here, we applied Molecular Cartography (MC, Resolve Biosciences), a multiplexed single-molecule hybridization method with submicron resolution (~136 nm), to create a spatial map of gene expression of the entire head and body of adult Drosophila melanogaster flies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Embryonic development had already been studied using SRT.
source: While embryonic development had already been studied using SRT (Wang et al., 2022), we present the first high-throughput smFISH-based SRT dataset of the various tissues of the adult fly.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: This study presents the first high-throughput smFISH-based SRT dataset of the various tissues of the adult fly.
source: While embryonic development had already been studied using SRT (Wang et al., 2022), we present the first high-throughput smFISH-based SRT dataset of the various tissues of the adult fly.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Expression patterns of 100 genes in the brain and 50 genes in the body can be visualized interactively using TissUUmaps at https://spatialfly.aertslab.org/.
source: Expression patterns of 100 genes in the brain and 50 genes in the body can be visualized interactively using TissUUmaps (Solorzano et al., 2020) at https://spatialfly.aertslab.org/.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: 50 genes were selected for the fly body samples based on expression data from the FCA.
source: Based on expression data from the FCA (Li et al., 2022; Pech et al., 2024) we selected 50 genes for the fly body samples, and 100 genes for the head samples given the large heterogeneity of neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: 100 genes were selected for the head samples given the large heterogeneity of neurons.
source: Based on expression data from the FCA (Li et al., 2022; Pech et al., 2024) we selected 50 genes for the fly body samples, and 100 genes for the head samples given the large heterogeneity of neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The selected genes cover a wide range of expression levels, from high to very low expressed genes.
source: These genes were carefully chosen to label the most important known cell types of the adult fly, and to include some unknown ones, suggested from the atlas data. They cover a wide range of expression levels, from high to very low expressed genes (Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section and supported by supplementary files and figures.

claim: An average of 190,622 mRNA molecules were detected for the head samples.
source: Using this workflow, we detected on average 190,622 mRNA molecules for the head samples (min = 101,548, max = 260,989), ranging from 56 (Poxn) to 23,439 (trio) mRNA molecules per gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B) and an average of 1.5 million mRNA molecules for the body samples (min = 1,448,593, max = 1,727,479), ranging from 112 (MsR1) to 510,619 (Act88F) mRNA molecules per gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: An average of 1.5 million mRNA molecules were detected for the body samples.
source: Using this workflow, we detected on average 190,622 mRNA molecules for the head samples (min = 101,548, max = 260,989), ranging from 56 (Poxn) to 23,439 (trio) mRNA molecules per gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B) and an average of 1.5 million mRNA molecules for the body samples (min = 1,448,593, max = 1,727,479), ranging from 112 (MsR1) to 510,619 (Act88F) mRNA molecules per gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: Neurons in the central and peripheral nervous system were identified using expression of elav and Syt1.

claim: The glial marker repo shows the location of glial cells across the body.
source: The glial marker repo shows the location of glial cells across the body (Figure 2A).

source: Interestingly, α- and β-Trypsin show distinct patterns, with β-Trypsin localized to the inner side of the gut, while α-Trypsin is more distal, suggesting a subcellular localization of these trypsin isoforms coding mRNAs to apical or basal regions of the gut enterocytes (Figure 2A).

claim: α-Trypsin is more distal in the gut compared to β-Trypsin.
source: Interestingly, α- and β-Trypsin show distinct patterns, with β-Trypsin localized to the inner side of the gut, while α-Trypsin is more distal, suggesting a subcellular localization of these trypsin isoforms coding mRNAs to apical or basal regions of the gut enterocytes (Figure 2A).

claim: The distinct patterns of α- and β-Trypsin suggest a subcellular localization of these trypsin isoforms coding mRNAs to apical or basal regions of the gut enterocytes.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Different populations of fat tissue and oenocytes were identified in the abdomen of the fly using AkhR and FASN2.
source: Using the fat body marker AkhR and the oenocyte marker FASN2, different populations of fat tissue and oenocytes were identified in the abdomen of the fly at the expected locations.

claim: The hemocyte marker Hml shows distinct local enrichments in the head, thorax, and abdomen.
source: The hemocyte marker Hml shows distinct local enrichments in the head, thorax, and abdomen (Figure 2A).

claim: LanB1 codes for LamininB1, an important component of the extracellular matrix present around many tissues.
source: In addition, LanB1, which codes for LamininB1, an important component of the extracellular matrix present around many tissues (Yarnitzky and Volk, 1995), is widely produced in different cell types and not only in hemocytes.

claim: LanB1 is widely produced in different cell types and not only in hemocytes.

claim: 15.5% of LanB1 co-expresses with Hml in hemocytes.
source: While co-expression of LanB1 with Hml in hemocytes is detected as reported (Matsubayashi et al., 2017) (15.5%) (Figure 2A), surprisingly most of LanB1 overlaps with epithelial cells (grh (13.4%) and pain (28.0%)) or muscle cells (Mlp84B (40.9%) and Mp20 (25.4%) (see Methods)).

claim: Most of LanB1 overlaps with epithelial cells or muscle cells.
source: While co-expression of LanB1 with Hml in hemocytes is detected as reported (Matsubayashi et al., 2017) (15.5%) (Figure 2A), surprisingly most of LanB1 overlaps with epithelial cells (grh (13.4%) and pain (28.0%)) or muscle cells (Mlp84B (40.9%) and Mp20 (25.4%) (see Methods)).

claim: The expression of esg in the sections is mostly limited to the gut, matching its reported expression in the intestinal stem cells.
source: The expression of esg in our sections is mostly limited to the gut, matching its reported expression in the intestinal stem cells (Jiang and Edgar, 2011) and the somatic cyst stem cells (Sênos Demarco et al., 2022; Figure 2A).

claim: Mhc and sls were used to label all muscle cells.

claim: TpnC4 and Act88F specifically label the IFMs.

claim: 99.7% of Act88F mRNA spots are detected in the expected regions of all body sections.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

source: In general, gene-gene correlations between SRT and snRNA-seq match significantly (r=0.69, p<1e-100), although there are some small biases between the techniques (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).

claim: Act88F is detected at higher numbers in SRT compared to snRNA-seq, which may be explained with differential mRNA stability in the cytoplasm.

claim: snRNA-seq is largely detecting nuclear-located mRNAs and thus rather monitors the transcriptional activity of the cell.

claim: sls mRNA is nucleus-enriched.

claim: TpnC4 mRNA is nucleus-depleted.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: mRNA distributions in cultured mammalian skeletal muscles were previously linked to mRNA sizes, with large mRNAs spreading further from the nuclei than small mRNAs.
source: Previously, mRNA distributions in cultured mammalian skeletal muscles were linked to mRNA sizes, with large mRNAs spreading further from the nuclei than small mRNAs (Pinheiro et al., 2021).

claim: The relationship between mRNA size and nuclear proximity does not seem to apply to the selected genes in this study.
source: This does not seem to apply to our selected genes, as sls mRNAs are significantly longer (isoform lengths: 15,263–56,489 nt) compared to TpnC4 (longest isoform: 859 nt) or TpnC41C mRNAs (longest isoform: 1,880 nt).

claim: sls mRNA forms large assemblies around nuclei close to the muscle-tendon junctions in the IFMs.
source: Furthermore, the nuclear enrichment of sls mRNA is not homogeneous across all nuclei, particularly in the IFMs, where sls mRNA forms large assemblies around nuclei close to the muscle-tendon junctions (Figure 4A–C).

claim: HCR-FISH confirmed the enrichment of sls mRNA around nuclei close to the muscle-tendon junctions.

claim: Some small differences were observed between MC and HCR, with sls mRNA enriched in broader regions around the muscle nuclei close to the tendons when detected with MC.

claim: In mammals, local enrichment of mRNA correlates with an accumulation of nuclei.

claim: No significant correlation was detected between the sls enrichment at the IFM ends and the nuclear DAPI signal.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: The terminal nuclei in IFMs may express higher levels of sls RNA than the central muscle nuclei.
source: In mammals, this local enrichment correlates with an accumulation of nuclei (Bruusgaard et al., 2003), however, we do not detect a significant correlation between the sls enrichment at the IFM ends and the nuclear DAPI signal (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and thus speculate that the terminal nuclei express higher levels of sls RNA than the central muscle nuclei.

claim: Act88F mRNA is enriched in the inter-myofibril space in the IFMs, where most nuclei, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi are located.

claim: TpnC4 and Mhc mRNAs appear enriched in complementary stripes at the location of the myofibrils and mitochondria in the IFMs.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: The spatial subdivision of flight muscles correlates with their intracellular architecture.

claim: A similar division was found in leg muscles, with central stripes of Act79B mRNA close to the nuclei while Mhc and TpnC41C mRNAs were enriched in the myofibril regions.

evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: HCR-FISH partially confirmed the anticorrelated expression patterns between Act88F and TpnC4 in IFMs.

claim: Act88F mRNA was found enriched in stripes along the rows of nuclei in IFMs by HCR-FISH, consistent with the MC data.

claim: TpnC4 mRNA was also found enriched in a few cases around nuclei by HCR-FISH.

claim: 13 sections of different fly heads were investigated, sectioned across the longitudinal direction, covering most regions of the fly head.
source: To investigate the localization of cell types in the adult Drosophila head, we investigated the 13 sections of different fly heads sectioned across the longitudinal direction, covering most regions of the fly head.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The diversity between sections originating from different brain regions is represented by lower correlations between the samples.
source: The diversity between sections originating from different brain regions is represented by lower correlations between the samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Different classes of cells were annotated using the marker genes para (neurons), alrm (astrocytes), and ninaC (photoreceptors).
source: Using the marker genes para (neurons), alrm (astrocytes), and ninaC (photoreceptors), we were able to annotate different classes of cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: ninaE was removed from the analysis due to being too highly expressed, leading to optical crowding.
source: ninaE, a second photoreceptor marker was too highly expressed, leading to optical crowding, and was removed from the analysis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Co-expression of C15, acj6, Oaz, caup, and unpg, markers for olfactory projection neurons (OPNs), is only detected in the most anterior samples.
source: We used the expression of C15, acj6, Oaz, caup, and unpg, markers for olfactory projection neurons (OPNs). OPNs relay information from the antennal lobe to downstream processing centers, including the mushroom body and the lateral horn. The co-expression of OPN markers is only detected in the most anterior samples, as expected (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: repo, moody, Indy, Vmat are markers for perineurial glia that form the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source: Next, we looked at repo, moody, Indy, Vmat, all of which are markers for perineurial glia that form the blood-brain barrier (BBB), and found them expressed at the periphery of the brain, consistent with the known location of the BBB (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: repo, moody, Indy, Vmat were found expressed at the periphery of the brain, consistent with the known location of the BBB.
source: Next, we looked at repo, moody, Indy, Vmat, all of which are markers for perineurial glia that form the blood-brain barrier (BBB), and found them expressed at the periphery of the brain, consistent with the known location of the BBB (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Gene-gene correlations between MC and snRNA-seq brain data show a strong match (r=0.68).
source: We compared gene-gene relationships, by calculating gene-gene correlations in MC and the snRNA-seq brain data (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B). In general, we find a strong match (r=0.68), however, there are also several mismatches.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: pros-dati co-expression is conserved between MC and snRNA-seq modalities.
source: While pros-dati co-expression is conserved between both modalities (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), co-expression of several other gene pairs is only detected in one modality (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Widespread expression of Vmat was only found in the BBB, but little or no expression in the central brain, where most dopaminergic neurons should be located.
source: For example, we only found widespread expression of Vmat in the BBB (stronger near the optic lobe), but little or no expression in the central brain, where most dopaminergic neurons should be located (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Vmat expression does not overlap with DAPI-stained nuclei or with DAT, suggesting an mRNA transport mechanism to locate selected mRNAs away from the cell body.
source: Additionally, Vmat expression does neither overlap with DAPI-stained nuclei nor with DAT (a marker for dopaminergic neurons), suggesting an mRNA transport mechanism to locate selected mRNAs away from the cell body (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Glial nuclei, which are much smaller than neuronal nuclei, might not all be detected with the methodology used.
source: Alternatively, glial nuclei, which are much smaller than neuronal nuclei (Mu et al., 2021), might not all be detected with our methodology.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The neuropeptides Ilp2 and Pdf show only a weak overlap with the DAPI staining, instead forming circular patterns.
source: Similarly, the neuropeptides Ilp2 and Pdf show only a weak overlap with the DAPI staining, instead forming circular patterns (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: There are 188 distinct clusters in the scRNA-seq dataset, of which only 83 are annotated.
source: In our scRNA-seq dataset, there are 188 distinct clusters, of which only 83 are annotated today.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Recent efforts to map the fly brain through EM and connectomics studies have identified 8453 morphological cell types.
source: Recent efforts to map the fly brain through EM and connectomics studies have identified 8453 morphological cell types (Dorkenwald et al., 2024; Schlegel et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: SRT can provide a bridge between scRNA-seq studies and morphology-based studies.
source: SRT can provide a bridge between scRNA-seq studies and morphology-based studies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Current neuronal nomenclature is based on neuropils (axons and dendrites) and not on the location of the neuronal nuclei.
source: It is important to note that current neuronal nomenclature is based on neuropils (axons and dendrites) and not on the location of the neuronal nuclei.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Fer1 is a strong marker for cluster 120 in the snRNA dataset.
source: To identify the location of uncharacterized clusters from the FCA in the brain, we started with Fer1 expression, as it is a strong marker for cluster 120 in our snRNA dataset (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Cells expressing Fer1 are located in the central brain, near the ventral gnathal ganglion and saddle, and the superior intermediate protocerebrum.
source: Using our MC data, we found that these cells are located in the central brain, near the ventral gnathal ganglion and saddle, and the superior intermediate protocerebrum (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: AstC expression (cluster 122) is limited to the dorsal part of the central brain, consistent with its expression in DN1 and DN3 neurons.
source: Furthermore, we show that AstC expression (cluster 122) is limited to the dorsal part of the central brain, consistent with its expression in DN1 and DN3 neurons (Díaz et al., 2019; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citation and figure.

claim: otp (clusters 30 and 62) marks nuclei close to the lateral horn and the superior neuropils.
source: Next, we investigated the expression of otp (clusters 30 and 62),which marks nuclei close to the lateral horn and the superior neuropils (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: vg (cluster 20) expression is limited to the boundary region between the optic lobe (OL) and the central brain (CB).
source: Finally, we determined the expression of vg (cluster 20) to be limited to the boundary region between the optic lobe (OL) and the central brain (CB) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Combining snRNA-seq with SRT technologies can identify defined locations of formerly uncharacterized cell clusters in the fly brain.
source: These results confirm that combining snRNA-seq with SRT technologies can indeed identify defined locations of formerly uncharacterized cell clusters in the fly brain.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Unsupervised clustering of brain MC data using all mRNA localizations from all datasets together identified 23 clusters.
source: By performing unsupervised clustering using all mRNA localizations from all datasets together, we identified 23 clusters (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Different slices display a different cluster composition, consistent with sectioning along the brain's A-P axis.
source: Different slices display a different cluster composition, consistent with our aim for sectioning along the brain's A-P axis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Photoreceptor genes such as ninaC and lz were strongly enriched in the retina.
source: As expected, photoreceptor genes such as ninaC and lz were strongly enriched in the retina.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: pros (CB) and scro (OL) expression creates a strong boundary clearly demarcating the optic lobe and central brain regions.
source: While many neuronal genes show similar expression between the OL and CB, pros (CB) and scro (OL) expression creates a strong boundary clearly demarcating the two anatomical regions (Figure 6G and H), corroborating earlier findings (Davie et al., 2018; Yoo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citations and figures.

claim: SRT alone can be used to identify specific markers for the major brain cell types or regional domains, without any prior knowledge.
source: This shows that SRT alone can be used to identify specific markers for the major brain cell types or regional domains, without any prior knowledge.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Some scRNA-seq clusters in the OL could be divided into ventral Wnt4 and dorsal Wnt10 positive subclusters.
source: Previously, it was shown that some scRNA-seq clusters in the OL could be divided into ventral Wnt4 and dorsal Wnt10 positive subclusters (Han et al., 2020; Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Wnt4 and Wnt10 mRNAs are strongly enriched in the ventral and dorsal regions of the brain, respectively.
source: Using Wnt4 and Wnt10 mRNA localizations we confirmed these findings and showed that, although expression is sparse, Wnt4 and Wnt10 mRNAs are strongly enriched in the ventral and dorsal regions of the brain, respectively (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: MC data of the fly brain allows the identification of clusters and cell types.
source: Altogether, our MC data of the fly brain allows the identification of clusters and cell types.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: SRT can be used to identify and localize unknown clusters of scRNA data, serving as a potential link between morphology data and single-cell data.
source: We also showed how SRT can be used to identify and localize unknown clusters of scRNA data, serving as a potential link between morphology data and single-cell data.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: SRT can be used for the discovery and confirmation of regional marker genes by performing region-based differential expression.
source: Finally, SRT can be used for the discovery and confirmation of regional marker genes by performing region-based differential expression.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Three different approaches were used and compared to represent SRT data: 5 μm-spaced grid rasterization, neighborhood embedding, and nuclei segmentation.
source: Here, we used and compared three different approaches to represent SRT data: 5 μm-spaced grid rasterization, neighborhood embedding, and nuclei segmentation (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: The grid and neighborhood embedding are both spatially unaware of the cell's location.
source: The grid and neighborhood embedding are both spatially unaware of the cell's location.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Neighborhood embedding makes it possible to visualize spatial patterns at subcellular resolution, but leads to a very large dataset and heavy computational load.
source: This makes it possible to also visualize spatial patterns at subcellular resolution, but leads to a very large dataset and heavy computational load (Partel and Wählby, 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The grid-based approach can be run in several hours, while neighborhood embedding takes several days.
source: While the grid-based approach can be run in several hours, neighborhood embedding takes several days.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Different densities of nuclei require imaging with different parameters to visualize both sparse and dense nuclei regions.
source: While this is the most intuitive method, several challenges occur in the fly head. To start, different densities of nuclei require imaging with different parameters to visualize both sparse and dense nuclei regions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The dense nuclei regions at the edge of the OL and CB are very difficult to segment with normal imaging techniques, with a strong overlap of cells and different cell types.
source: In addition, the dense nuclei regions at the edge of the OL and CB are very difficult to segment with normal imaging techniques, with a strong overlap of cells and different cell types (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Lasso regression, Tangram, and SpaGE were applied to compare label transfer methods.
source: To compare label transfer methods we applied lasso regression, Tangram, and SpaGE.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Regression-based integration in the grid method and SpaGE in the neighborhood embedding method can match the blood-brain barrier and the chiasm glia in the optic lobe very well.
source: We found that regression-based integration in the grid method and SpaGE in the neighborhood embedding method can match the blood-brain barrier and the chiasm glia in the optic lobe very well, together with astrocytes and ensheathing glia in the central brain (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: The nuclei segmentation method performs poorly for matching glial subtypes, since most of the glial nuclei are not detected.
source: In contrast, the nuclei segmentation method performs poorly for matching glial subtypes, since most of the glial nuclei are not detected, leading to the removal of most glial mRNAs (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: All methods can accurately identify neurons from the different layers in the OL.
source: In the OL, all methods can accurately identify neurons from the different layers.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Both the grid-based and the segmentation methods are able to locate the peptidergic neurons (insulin-producing cells, Pdf-neurons) in the correct location in the CB.
source: In the CB, both the grid-based and the segmentation methods are able to locate the peptidergic neurons (insulin-producing cells, Pdf-neurons) in the correct location, while neighborhood embedding fails to retrieve these (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: Neighborhood embedding fails to retrieve peptidergic neurons in the CB.
source: In the CB, both the grid-based and the segmentation methods are able to locate the peptidergic neurons (insulin-producing cells, Pdf-neurons) in the correct location, while neighborhood embedding fails to retrieve these (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: Tangram labels some non-peptidergic segmented nuclei as insulin-producing unless thresholds for mapping scores are manually adjusted.
source: However, Tangram also labels some non-peptidergic segmented nuclei as insulin-producing unless thresholds for mapping scores are manually adjusted to reflect the different proportions of cell types that are present in the MC data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Nuclei segmentation and grid methods are able to identify the Kenyon cells of the mushroom body in a more posterior CB sample.
source: In a more posterior CB sample, nuclei segmentation and grid methods are able to identify the Kenyon cells of the mushroom body.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Kenyon cells are found in the neighborhood embedding, but the signal is noisier.
source: These are also found in the neighborhood embedding, but the signal is noisier (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Neighborhood embedding likely performs poorly on cell types that are determined by high expression of only 1 gene.
source: Neighborhood embedding likely performs poorly on cell types that are determined by high expression of only 1 gene (e.g. neuropeptides), since one gene only has a marginal effect on the neighborhood.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The grid and neighborhood embedding methods spatially localized two uncharacterized clusters.
source: The grid and neighborhood embedding methods spatially localized two uncharacterized clusters, while the nuclei segmentation method spatially localized four clusters (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: The nuclei segmentation method spatially localized four uncharacterized clusters.
source: The grid and neighborhood embedding methods spatially localized two uncharacterized clusters, while the nuclei segmentation method spatially localized four clusters (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Cluster 20, which was marked by vg expression, is found by each technique.
source: Cluster 20, which was marked by vg expression, is found by each technique (Figures 6E and 7F), same as cluster 79.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figures.

claim: Cluster 79 is located to the outside of the retina, fitting with high expression of Cpr72Ec, a structural protein for the eye lens, which is expressed by interommatidial pigment cells.
source: Cluster 79 is located to the outside of the retina, fitting with high expression of Cpr72Ec, a structural protein for the eye lens, which is expressed by interommatidial pigment cells (Stahl et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Tangram detected a ventral-dorsal division in the retina, with cluster 15 matching to the dorsal part.
source: In contrast to the other methods, Tangram detected a ventral-dorsal division in the retina, with cluster 15 matching to the dorsal part.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The mapping of cluster 15 to the dorsal part of the retina is driven by the expression of mirr, a gene known to be expressed in the dorsal half of the eye.
source: This mapping is driven by the expression of mirr, a gene known to be expressed in the dorsal half of the eye (McNeill et al., 1997; Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting citation and figure.

claim: Tangram maps cluster 69, mostly by expression of caup.
source: Tangram also maps cluster 69, mostly by expression of caup.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: caup is detected in the dorsal half of the eye and shows additional expression in various locations in the central brain.
source: Like its Iroquouis family member mirr, caup is also detected in the dorsal half of the eye, however, it shows additional expression in various locations in the central brain (Figure 7—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section with supporting figure.

claim: Using a 5 µm by 5 µm grid leads to similar clustering results as performing a computationally heavy neighborhood embedding analysis.
source: To conclude, we found that using a 5 µm by 5 µm grid leads to similar clustering results as performing a computationally heavy neighborhood embedding analysis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The neighborhood embedding increases the resolution to single mRNA spots, leading to a better visualization and a higher spatial accuracy.
source: However, the neighborhood embedding does increase the resolution to single mRNA spots, leading to a better visualization and a higher spatial accuracy.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The nuclei segmentation method is limited in the fly brain by the inability of the DAPI signal to resolve overlapping individual nuclei in very densely packed brain regions.
source: The nuclei segmentation method is limited in the fly brain by the inability of the DAPI signal to resolve overlapping individual nuclei in very densely packed brain regions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Tangram was the best method to identify unknown clusters.
source: While Tangram was the best method to identify unknown clusters, it also led to false-positive labeling of multiple cell types, leading to the necessity of accurate thresholding.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Tangram led to false-positive labeling of multiple cell types, leading to the necessity of accurate thresholding.
source: While Tangram was the best method to identify unknown clusters, it also led to false-positive labeling of multiple cell types, leading to the necessity of accurate thresholding.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Using a simple regression model works as well or even better as designated methods when marker genes are used, while running much faster.
source: We find that using a simple regression model works as well or even better as designated methods when marker genes are used, while running much faster.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: A consensus of different methods is suggested to optimally integrate scRNA-seq data with SRT.
source: Therefore, we suggest relying on a consensus of different methods to optimally integrate scRNA-seq data with SRT.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: This study presents the first SRT dataset of the adult fly brain and body using a highly multiplexed single molecular in situ hybridization technique Molecular Cartography (MC).
source: Here, we present the first SRT dataset of the adult fly brain and body using a highly multiplexed single molecular in situ hybridization technique Molecular Cartography (MC).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: Most of the published classical mRNA in situ hybridizations used the more easily accessible fly embryos.
source: Most of the published classical mRNA in situ hybridizations (Tomancak et al., 2002; Lécuyer et al., 2007; Jambor et al., 2015), as well as a recent high throughput FISH study used the more easily accessible fly embryos (Wang et al., 2022), We expanded SRT here to the more complex anatomy of the adult fly, which requires sectioning and large data sampling, both at the microscope and at the computer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Using a 50-genes panel in the body, all major cell types in the adult male fly were identified.
source: Using a 50-genes panel in the body, all major cell types in the adult male fly were identified.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: The expression of key markers was sufficient to locate rare cell populations in the adult body.
source: Furthermore, the expression of key markers was sufficient to locate rare cell populations in the adult body.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: A high concordance with published snRNA-seq data was shown using several measures of co-expression.
source: We further showed a high concordance with published snRNA-seq data using several measures of co-expression (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: In flies both the brain and the whole-body can be sliced and imaged, allowing an unprecedented whole body view.
source: While SRT based on smFISH in mice (Yao et al., 2023) and humans (Fang et al., 2022) is currently limited to a single tissue, in flies both the brain and the whole-body can be sliced and imaged, allowing an unprecedented whole body view.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Many markers are highly specific to certain cell types, as quantified for Act88F and TpnC4 for the flight muscles (>99% specificity).
source: We found that many markers are indeed highly specific to certain cell types, as we quantified for Act88F and TpnC4 for the flight muscles (>99% specificity), which is consistent with previous benchmarks of MC in human and mouse cells (Groiss et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: Some marker genes showed additional unexpected expression that was not detected in snRNA-seq.
source: Still, some marker genes showed additional unexpected expression (e.g. expression of tin and TpnC4 in the ejaculatory bulb muscles), which was not detected in snRNA-seq.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: Widespread expression of LanB1 was observed in various cell types, beyond just hemocytes.
source: Additionally, we observed widespread expression of LanB1 in various cell types, beyond just hemocytes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: SRT can provide a more sensitive readout, including the spatial localization.
source: As such, SRT can provide a more sensitive readout, including the spatial localization, and may inspire which other tissues might be interesting to investigate in the future when studying a particular gene function.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: A 100-genes panel in the head was sufficient to identify the major classes of cell types in the brain, including some very specific neuronal cell types.
source: In the head, we used a 100-genes panel and showed that this selection is sufficient to identify the major classes of cell types in the brain, including some very specific neuronal cell types like peptidergic neurons, Kenyon cells, and different OL neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: By using informative markers enriched in previously uncharacterized clusters from single-cell RNA-seq data, the nuclei in the fly brain that express these markers were pinpointed.
source: Furthermore, by using informative markers enriched in previously uncharacterized clusters from single-cell RNA-seq data, we were able to pinpoint the nuclei in the fly brain that express these markers.

claim: The next challenge lies in connecting nuclei to the neuronal connectome using connectomics studies.
source: The next challenge lies in connecting these nuclei to the neuronal connectome using connectomics studies (Schlegel et al., 2024), in order to unambiguously identify the individual cell types.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: In Drosophila, neuronal nomenclature and cell typing focus on projections, instead of nuclei localization.
source: Indeed, in Drosophila, neuronal nomenclature and cell typing focus on projections, instead of nuclei localization.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Discussion section.

claim: Future large-scale SRT data can serve as a bridge between different modalities to link scRNA-seq atlases with spatial information, including connectomics in the brain.
source: We believe that future large-scale SRT data can serve as a bridge between different modalities, similar to the Rosetta stone, to link scRNA-seq atlases with spatial information, including connectomics in the brain.

source: The first issue is technical, since the small area of the head made it difficult to achieve homogeneous adhesion to the slides, leading to significant deformation of the samples.

claim: The small and dense Drosophila brain nuclei are hard to segment (average size 5 cubic micrometers).

source: A possible solution would be to use SRT-compatible expansion microscopy (Fan et al., 2023; Pownall et al., 2023; Steib et al., 2022).

source: Alternatively, imaging techniques that allow super-resolution like DNA-PAINT, could help to achieve higher resolution (sub 5 nm resolution) (Agasti et al., 2017; Schueder et al., 2023).

source: Given the dense packing of the small nuclei in the fly brain, and the likely presence of mRNA transport away from the nucleus of origin, nuclei-segmentation leads to a loss of information compared to the other nuclei-unaware techniques.

source: Therefore, we predict strong improvements when using larger gene panels.

source: It was previously reported in the embryo that large numbers of mRNAs are non-homogeneously distributed and thus likely transported (Jambor et al., 2015; Lécuyer et al., 2007; Tomancak et al., 2002).
